You can just buy a firearm from a private seller. You will need to show your ID (unless you run into a similar transaction to a few I have done) and often they will want to take down your info, that is normal, you should also take theirs down (in case it is stolen or the like).

If you go the dealer route, then your form 4473 will be held on by the dealer for at least 20 years IIRC, often longer, and if that dealer goes out of business, the ATF likes to gobble up those papers (most of my firearms were bought this way, it's not that big of a deal IMHO because they would have to search through millions of said forms, and there are always 'boating accidents' to account for).

The fully legal and 100% off the books, or mostly because your credit card or some bill of sale for the parts will be a form of record, you can get a 80% lower for an AR or glock and build the gun yourself, or alternative you can just build your own gun from anything. Now you can not legally sell this home made gun or the ATF will really come down on your ass because they want their manufacturing FFL fees, though in theory you could sell all the parts but the receiver and crush it to get rid of it... but you won't get shit for used gun parts unless they are something special anyway.

Polymer80 for a Glock lower. It is a serialized but 80% finished part that counts as a piece of plastic, legally.

All other parts can probably be legally purchased without registration, depending on your state laws of course. Assembling it is an excellent learning experience and teaches patience and maintenance of the tool, so when something breaks later, which is rare for Glocks anyway, you will now exactly how to repair it with a cheap and readily available spare part for a few dollars.

Same goes for AR lowers. The CNC machine needed for it can be had used and resold later for almost the same price, costing only the transaction costs.

Do not CNC machine any part for someone other than yourself, though. That is illegal. Give them the machine and your advices only. That way, others also have to build the skill and patience to do so.
